project.name: DermaScope
project.context: Browser-first facial skin signal mapping from one uploaded or captured face photo.
project.domain: Single-photo face-skin signal mapping with lithographic color-separation plate overlay, scores, and face zones.
project.runtimeConstraint: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI frontend with FastAPI-backed OpenCV-Python analysis.
project.architectureConstraint: Client-side SPA submits one image to /api/process and receives overlay PNG plus X-DermaScope-Analysis metadata without persistent image storage.

assumptions: DermaScope is production-facing and reports visible image-processing signals without medical diagnosis, treatment, or product recommendations.
The input flow supports file upload and browser camera capture.
The backend may be offline, so service readiness must remain visible.

productReading.productTypeAndCoreVerb: DermaScope is a browser-first facial skin signal mapping app; the user submits one face photo and inspects mapped visible signals.
highestStakesUserMoments: Intake must make file limits, privacy, camera permission, and face-photo requirements clear before the user shares an image.
Processing must show service readiness and a non-diagnostic status while the backend analyzes the photo.
Results must connect overlay marks, category scores, and zones so users understand what the algorithm measured.
productReading.dominantDataShapes: The screen is dominated by one spatial image, five condition categories, and five face zones.
productReading.latencyProfile: Analysis is soft real-time: a single request returns a PNG overlay and metadata after processing.
productReading.failureModes: The UI must absorb offline backend, invalid image, oversized image, camera permission failure, processing failure, fallback face detection, stale result risk, and missing or malformed analysis metadata.
productReading.contextOfUse: The app is a sustained single-task inspection flow, not a feed, stored history product, or admin monitor.
productReading.knownConstraints: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI are present; WCAG 2.2 AA, no persistent image storage, safe errors, and no medical diagnosis are hard constraints.

motionPaletteDecision.anchorReference: Fine-art lithography print registration sheet (color-separation plates)
motionPaletteDecision.signatureMotionBehavior: A mechanical plate slide overlays the image channels, settling with a micro-vibration convergence at 240ms, while aside indicators stagger in sequentially.
motionPaletteDecision.paletteDecision: Sheet structure is warm tactile ivory; frame boundaries are high-density carbon-black; separation inks are process vermilion, umber, cobalt, rhodamine, and viridian.
motionPaletteDecision.typographicRoleContrast: Heavy ink-rich serif display headings pair with high-legibility geometric sans body copy and tabular technical monospace for print calibration metrics.

visualResetStrategy.resetReason: The user explicitly requested a redesign with a concept that must differ from both the previous topographic survey plate and the older conservation map direction.
discardedContinuity: survey-paper, safety orange, cyan waterline, and olive terrain palette

conceptualAnchor.name: Fine-art lithography print registration sheet
conceptualAnchor.anchorReference: Fine-art lithography print registration sheet (color-separation plates)
conceptualAnchor.specificReferencePoint: A manual printmaking registration bed where separate ink-plates are aligned using mechanical crosshairs, color-bars, and ink density draw-downs to compile a single cohesive print.
conceptualAnchor.rationale: Treats each skin-condition signal as a distinct color-separation plate layer that aligns onto the base key face photo. The layout uses alignment crosshairs, registration markers, ink density meters, and tactile press margins to arrange scores and face zones without dashboard or clinical clichés.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMotion: Tactile plate alignment and micro-vibration crosshair convergence
conceptualAnchor.signatureMove: The single face image is held inside a carbon-black metal plate holder with registration marks in the margins. Toggling an overlay triggers a mechanical sliding animation of the plate into exact alignment.
conceptualAnchor.typographicDecision: An ink-heavy elegant display serif (Lora) for editorial press headings is paired with Outfit for Indonesian product copy, and a technical monospace (IBM Plex Mono) for plate numbers, alignment coordinates, and density metrics.

derivedTokenLogic.anchorReference: Fine-art lithography print registration sheet (color-separation plates)
derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Fine-art printmaking inks: natural warm ivory paper base, dense carbon black press frame, and process vermilion, umber, cobalt, rhodamine, and viridian plate colors.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Tactile print margins, plate register steps, and mechanical guide bars, using a clean 16px structural base with standard 44px touch targets.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Tactile editorial print title, geometric press copy, and tabular plate numbers drive Lora/Outfit/IBM Plex Mono roles.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Manual plate registration, crosshair convergence vibration, and sequential press bed lowering.
derivedTokenLogic.colorSpace: sRGB CSS variables with high-contrast OKLCH-safe lightness targets.
derivedTokenLogic.typeScaleMethod: Fixed role sizes with fluid editorial clamp for titles; no dynamic scale for technical metrics.
derivedTokenLogic.motionBudget: 150-300ms for micro-interactions, 350ms maximum for manual plate registration slide, reduced-motion fallbacks required.
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Tokens must satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, include distinct plate marker shapes (non-color-only), and completely avoid neobrutalist brutal survey tokens.

aiSafeUiAudit.paletteEvidence: The palette maps condition categories to authentic printmaker inks (vermilion, umber, cobalt, rhodamine, viridian) rather than skincare pastel glow or clinical blue sterile calmness.
aiSafeUiAudit.nonTransferableBehavior: Ink plate registration alignment marks, ink draw-downs, and plate density meters attach strictly to printmaking compilation, making no sense on generic web dashboards or beauty apps.
